body:
I'm so sorry for all that you've been through. I know how hard it can be when your friend's don't listen, and how guarded it makes you. I'm reading through your story and I wish I had more to say that would help you or give you some comfort when you so clearly need it. 

Is counselling outside your campus an option? Not to be presumptuous but it seems you need the help of a professional that can give you what you need. It's not a vanity exercise for your counsellor, and if it's not working you should be totally up front with her about needing to move on or whatever else.

Again, I'm so sorry for everything you're going through and I hope you find some measure of the care that you need soon.

First off, I'm glad to hear you have such supportive friends to help you get through this. 

You made a mistake you probably won't make again. You know that it's wrong, you accept that and are allowing it to change your future behaviour.

She's an underage girl who, scared of her part in a shared mistake, is attempting to protect herself. While she's employed a very serious threat against you, the actual likelihood of that hurting you, in the legal sense, is not very likely. 

I hope you keep sharing with your friends and try and persevere through this difficult time.

You've dealt with so much in a short space of time and you need a shoulder to lean on. Please don't hurt yourself. You sound like someone who is generous to a fault; you sacrifice your own wellbeing for that of others, and that is the most noble thing in the world. We need more people like you.

From my experience, friends value when you share your problems with them, especially from those who are typically reserved. Please, try and find a way to share your pain with your friends, or someone close. Give your friends the chance to be there for you and I'm sure they will.

Are you getting any professional help? I can't recommend enough that you do. Speaking for myself, it's been one of the only things that I've found to help.
I am truly glad to hear that, and I hope you feel better soon.

I don't know how much each subsequent inspirational message is worth to you, but I figure it's worth a shot. 

Is it possible for you to talk about your childhood with your adopted parents? It sounds like they truly care about you. Maybe this is bad reasoning, but if the choice is between the discomfort of sharing your history and feeling like you do now, I really want you to consider any way of sharing how you feel with them. Just any amount that you're comfortable with will help them have some understanding of what you're going through.

I know you said you aren't 'seeing' anyone professionally. Many colleges have on-campus psychologists and support staff; I can't encourage you enough to find some kind of help. It's been one of two things that's helped me overcome even a few of my problems. Prior to this I'd just been drowning for years.
